title: 4WD/AWD binds or chatters in tight turns on dry pavement (transfer case fluid, not tires)

beats.prompt: macro close up shot of a car transfer case housing between the front and rear driveshafts on the underside of an SUV, sunlight catching the metal casing, subtle engine idle vibration, shallow depth of field, photorealistic
beats.vo: Your 4WD or AWD binding up in tight turns? That's probably not your tires.

beats.shot: Bird's-eye drone shot of an SUV tracing a tight, complete circle in an empty parking lot at full lock
beats.prompt: bird's eye drone style shot of an SUV slowly tracing a tight complete circle in an empty parking lot at full steering lock, tire contact patches visibly scrubbing sideways against dry pavement, photorealistic
beats.vo: A shudder, hop, or binding feeling in a slow, tight turn — usually noticed in a parking lot or driveway on dry pavement.

beats.shot: Object-only cutaway of a transfer case gear-and-chain assembly, front and rear output shafts rotating at slightly different speeds
beats.prompt: object only technical cutaway of an open car transfer case gear and chain assembly, front and rear output shafts rotating at slightly different speeds, clean diagrammatic lighting, slow orbiting camera move, no text or labels, photorealistic
beats.vo: That points to your transfer case or center differential — the part that lets all four wheels travel different paths in a turn.

beats.shot: Two dishes side by side, clean amber gear oil vs. dark metal-flecked gear oil, slow rack-focus
beats.prompt: close up comparison of two shallow dishes side by side under even studio light, one holding clean amber gear oil, the other holding dark metal fleck flecked gear oil, slow rack focus between them, no hands present, photorealistic
beats.vo: Old or low transfer case fluid can make that binding worse, and pushing through it again and again wears the drivetrain faster.

beats.shot: Shop inspection light sweeping across a transfer case fill-plug bolt with a faint oil weep line
beats.prompt: a shop inspection light on a stand sweeps its beam across a car transfer case housing fill plug bolt, threads and a faint oil weep line visible under the light, no hands present, slow rack focus, photorealistic
beats.vo: One clue is not a diagnosis — worth having the transfer case fluid checked before a tight parking lot turn becomes a bigger repair.

igfbCopy.primaryCaption: Your 4WD or AWD binding up when you turn tight? It's probably not your tires. That shudder or hop in a slow, tight turn on dry pavement usually points to the transfer case or center differential, not tread, not alignment. Old or low transfer case fluid can make it worse over time. Stop by and we'll take a look.

adVariants.caption: That bind or hop in a tight, slow turn is a driveline clue, not a tire clue. Here's the 30-second parking-lot way to tell.
